About this item

  • 【2025 UPGRADED ACASIS Hybrid USB A&C 3.2 Hub】Features 16 ports (8 USB-A 3.2 Ports+8 USB-C 3.2 Ports) with 10Gbps transfer speed, delivering faster connections and less waiting. Handle massive files and multitask with ease, backed by extensive testing in the lab showing speeds of W: 1008.9MB/s, R: 860.7MB/s. Note: Powered usb c hub do not support video output function.
  • 【96W Powered USB 3.2 Hub】With a 96W power adapter, the usb hub supports multiple devices at once(up to 5V/1.5A) which is sufficient to charge USB devices. It includes surge protection, hot swapping, and is safe for your Mac, phone, and tablet. Certified with FCC, UL, CE, and UKCA.
  • 【Aluminium Alloy Housing】ACASIS usb port hub build with quality aluminium alloy, ensuring quick heat dissipation and durability. It assurances stable connections with multiple devices, preventing overheating and disconnections, and is drop-resistant.
  • 【Independent Switch】ACASIS 16-port USB 3.2 hub features independent switches for each 10Gbps port, providing enhanced security and convenience by allowing direct activation without unplugging cables.
  • 【Wide Compatibility】The usb hub with power is compatible with most operating systems: Windows XP/Vista/7/8/10/11, MacOS-8/9/X, Linux. It ensures fast PLUG-AND-PLAY installation, allowing you to easily connect and use your devices across different systems.
  • 【Packaging contents】1xACASIS Hybrid USB 3.2 Hub, 1 x 96W Power Adapter, 1 x 3.3ft USB-A to USB-C/A cable and 1 user manual. With a 24-month pleasant customer service and fre* replacement if there is any quality issue.
  • 【Original Equipment Manufacturer】ACASIS product series includes Multi-port USB Hub, 40Gbps NVMe Enclosure, Capture Card and so on are widely Praised by Wholesalers and Customers. Since 2008, ACASIS has becoming a company that integrates research and development, design, production and sales. Our mission is to help more people solve video and data transmission problems by bringing stable, reliable and easy-to-use technology to users around the world.

How customer reviews and ratings work

Customer Reviews, including Product Star Ratings help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

    5 out of 5 stars
    The best USB hub out there. Worth every dollar.
    Reviewed in the United States on March 7, 2026
    Color: Gray
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    This hub is pleasing beyond expectations. I bought one six weeks ago, and when it didn't fail during my 30 day return window I bought another. It's now a week later and all is well, and if nothing breaks, my opinion is that this is the best thing out there.

    It's got 8 USB-C ports, 7 USB-A ports, a massive power supply, and switches that are not mechanical on/off, in/out push-buttons but light-press switches (no clicks) with blue indicator lights. The chassis is metal and you feel that you own a quality device. I'm using one on a Mac mini and the other on a big gaming PC. On both machines I went from messy spaghetti to nice and tidy.

    I just re-read the 1-star reviews and I haven't experienced any of those issues, USB-PD issues and ports not working. But I do have several USB-powered MIDI devices that small, un-powered USB hubs could not handle at all (I bought five, hoping one would work), presumably because they couldn't supply enough power, and this one was the fix. It works fine for "normal" devices, like external drives and SSDs, other hubs, and my MIDI stuff. Devices requiring massive power I haven't tried but my neither do I need them on my desk. They have their own power supplies.

  • Derek
    1 out of 5 stars
    Inconsistent, unreliable, and unfortunately disappointing
    Reviewed in the United States on February 3, 2026
    Color: Gray
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I hate to say it, but this hub (at least the one I received) is garbage.

    I will give the manufacturer points for build quality, the hub seems to built well and using quality materials. Unfortunately, that's about where the positive news ends and as far as usability goes I cannot recommend this device. I've listed below the problems I experienced within the first 24 hours of usage:

    1) The switches outright just do not work for many devices. I tried several devices which seem to somehow just "ignore" the switch being turned off. I put ignore in quotes, because the device should not be built in a way that would allow any attached device to communicate with the host while it's off. For some devices, the switch does work correctly. However, for other devices, I can plug a USB cable into the hub and have it persistently connected to the host no matter how many times I toggle the switch on and off. This is a key indicator that the device was not designed in a secure way. When the toggle switch is off, power and connectivity should be completely disconnected to the port. The fact that I am able to bypass the toggle switch is an indicator that some sort of firmware workaround is being used. Bad news here.

    2) Power delivery does not seem to work correctly on the hub. I'm using the power adapter that was delivered with the device which is plugged into a stable power source. Some devices which require power delivery (USB-PD) get stuck in an initializing state when drawing power from the hub. They get enough power to appear powered on, but the device never initializes and the host system can detect something was plugged in but cannot interface with the device. When I switch these devices to a different hub (or directly to the host), the issue is not present and the device works as expected.

    3) Even devices that do connect, seem to have issues with performance and/or connectivity. When some devices are attached to the hub, the host operating system seems to hang while the device is connecting. I experience this on about 1/3 of my attempts with any mass storage device, and some devices fairly consistently. When I do get a device to connect to the host, my transfer speeds are considerably lower than if I had used a different hub or connected directly to the host.

    All in all, I absolutely do not recommend this device. There are several clear indicators of poor and unsafe design when it comes to this hub, and I would not trust that it delivers power cleanly or that there's any consistent integrity on file transfers.

    Again, all of these issues were experienced within the first 24 hours of usage. I tested over a dozen different devices with this hub, of varying types and manufacturer. If I had this many issues straight away, I can guarantee it's not an isolated incident. Even if my hub was "defective", there's no way it would have been defective in a way that would selectively allow some devices to connect while toggled off.

    Let this be a warning to you!
